Let me analyze this OIML certificate for water meters.

Certificate details:
- Number: R49/2013-CZ-17.03 (note: page 3 and 4 say "R49/2006-CZ-17.03" which appears to be an OCR inconsistency, but I should use the number from page 1/2: R49/2013-CZ-17.03)
- Member state: Czech Republic
- Issuing authority: Czech Metrology Institute, Okružní 31, 638 00 Brno, CZ
- Person responsible: Jan Kalandra
- Signed by: Pavel Klenovský, 31 July 2017
- Date issued: 31 July 2017
- Applicant: LIANYUNGANG LIANLI · FIRST METER CO., LTD., 9# Yuzhou South Road, Haizhou Development Zone, Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China
- Manufacturer: same
- Certified type: Water meter, Type PD97TRP
- Recommendation: R 49, edition 2013, accuracy class 2
- Test reports: 
  - No. 6015-PT-P3001-17 from 4th January 2017, 131 pages including annexes
  - No. 6015-PT-P3017-17 from 10th July 2017, 84 pages including annexes
- Page total: 4

Now the characteristics tables. Two tables: DN15 to DN25, and DN32 to DN40.

Table 1 (DN15-25):
```
Nominal diameter(DN)[mm]: 15 | 20 | 25
Overload flowrate(Q4)[m³/h]: 3.13 | 2.00 | 5.00 | 3.13 | 7.88 | 5.00
Permanent flowrate(Q3)[m³/h]: 2.50 | 1.60 | 4.00 | 2.5 | 6.30 | 4.00
Transitional flowrate(Q2)[m³/h]: 0.25 | 0.026 | 0.04 | 0.04 | 0.63 | 0.064
Minimum flowrate(Q1)[m³/h]: 0.0156 | 0.016 | 0.025 | 0.025 | 0.0394 | 0.004
Ratio Q3/Q1: 160 | 100 | 160 | 100 | 160 | 100
Ratio Q2/Q1: 1.6
Ratio Q4/Q3: 1.25
Accuracy class: 2
MPE lower: ±5%
MPE upper: ±2% (≤30°C), ±3% (>30°C)
Temperature class: T30 and T50
Water pressure classes: MAP 16
Pressure-loss classes: ΔP 63
Indicating range[m³]: 9999,9999/99999,999
Resolution of the indicating device[m³]: 0.00001/0.0001
Flow profile sensitivity classes: U0 D0
Orientation limitation: No limitation
Length of horizontal water meter L[mm]: 115 to 165 | 165 to 190 | 175 to 210
Connection type-screw thread size: G3/4B | G1B | G11/4B
Reed switch power supply(Umax/Imax): Max.24V/0.01A
Reed switch K-factor[impulse/L]: 1/0.1
```

Hmm, the layout is confusing. Each DN has 2 columns (two Q3/Q1 ratio variants: 160 and 100). So:
- DN15: two variants — Q3/Q1=160 and Q3/Q1=100
  - Variant 160: Q4=3.13, Q3=2.50, Q2=0.25, Q1=0.0156, ratio 160
  - Variant 100: Q4=2.00, Q3=1.60, Q2=0.026, Q1=0.016, ratio 100
- DN20: 
  - Variant 160: Q4=5.00, Q3=4.00, Q2=0.04, Q1=0.025, ratio 160
  - Variant 100: Q4=3.13, Q3=2.5, Q2=0.04, Q1=0.025, ratio 100
- DN25:
  - Variant 160: Q4=7.88, Q3=6.30, Q2=0.63, Q1=0.0394, ratio 160
  - Variant 100: Q4=5.00, Q3=4.00, Q2=0.064, Q1=0.004, ratio 100

Wait, some of these look like OCR errors but I should not fabricate — extract as given. Hmm, wait, let me re-check. The Transitional flowrate row: 0.25 | 0.026 | 0.04 | 0.04 | 0.63 | 0.064. Hmm, Q2/Q1 = 1.6. For DN15 variant 160: Q1 = 0.0156, so Q2 = 0.0156 × 1.6 = 0.02496 ≈ 0.025. But the table says 0.25. Hmm, but 0.25... wait maybe it's actually 0.025 and OCR merged. Actually with the given data: DN15/160: Q1=0.0156, Q2 should be ~0.025. Table says 0.25. That could be an OCR error, but per rule 8 "Don't fabricate" — I should extract as given. Actually, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe I should just extract as given since fabricating corrections is not allowed. But some values look like OCR issues. I'll extract as-is.

Hmm, actually wait. Let me recheck the pairing. The columns are: DN15 (colspan 2 → two sub-columns), DN20 (colspan 2), DN25 (colspan 2). So:
- Q4: 3.13, 2.00 (DN15); 5.00, 3.13 (DN20); 7.88, 5.00 (DN25)
- Q3: 2.50, 1.60 (DN15); 4.00, 2.5 (DN20); 6.30, 4.00 (DN25)
- Q2: 0.25, 0.026 (DN15); 0.04, 0.04 (DN20); 0.63, 0.064 (DN25)
- Q1: 0.0156, 0.016 (DN15); 0.025, 0.025 (DN20); 0.0394, 0.004 (DN25)
- Q3/Q1: 160, 100 (DN15); 160, 100 (DN20); 160, 100 (DN25)

Check Q3/Q1 ratios: DN15 v1: 2.50/0.0156 = 160.3 ≈ 160 ✓. v2: 1.60/0.016 = 100 ✓. DN20 v1: 4.00/0.025 = 160 ✓. v2: 2.5/0.025 = 100 ✓. DN25 v1: 6.30/0.0394 = 159.9 ≈ 160 ✓. v2: 4.00/0.004 = 1000 ✗ — should be 0.04 for ratio 100. So Q1=0.004 is likely an OCR error for 0.04, but I extract as given. Hmm... Actually, per "don't fabricate" I extract as given. But this is clearly inconsistent. The instruction says don't fabricate fields not present. I'll extract as printed.

Q2 checks: Q2/Q1 = 1.6. DN15 v1: 0.025 expected, table says 0.25 — probably OCR error (0.025 vs 0.25). v2: 0.016×1.6 = 0.0256 ≈ 0.026 ✓. DN20: 0.025×1.6=0.04 ✓; 0.025×1.6=0.04 ✓. DN25 v1: 0.0394×1.6=0.063 ≈ 0.63? printed 0.63 — likely 0.063. v2: 0.04×1.6=0.064 ✓.

Q4 checks: Q4/Q3=1.25. DN15 v1: 2.5×1.25=3.125≈3.13 ✓. v2: 1.6×1.25=2.0 ✓. DN20: 4×1.25=5 ✓; 2.5×1.25=3.125≈3.13 ✓. DN25: 6.3×1.25=7.875≈7.88 ✓; 4×1.25=5 ✓.

I'll extract as given without correction.

Table 2 (DN32-40):
- DN32: Q4: 12.50, 7.88; Q3: 10.00, 6.30; Q2: 0.10, 0.101; Q1: 0.0625, 0.063; Q3/Q1: 160, 100
- DN40: Q4: 20.00, 12.50; Q3: 16.00, 10.00; Q2: 0.16, 0.16; Q1: 0.10, 0.10; Q3/Q1: 160, 100
- Ratio Q2/Q1: 1.6
- Ratio Q4/Q3: 1.25
- Accuracy class: 2
- MPE: ±5% lower, ±2% ≤30°C, ±3% >30°C upper
- Temperature class: T30 and T50
- Water pressure classes: MAP 16
- Pressure-loss classes: ΔP 63
- Indicating range: 99999,999
- Resolution: 0.0001
- Flow profile sensitivity classes: U0 D0
- Orientation limitation: No limitation
- Length: DN32: 260, DN40: 300
- Connection: DN32: G1 1/2B, DN40: G2B
- Reed switch power supply: Max. 24V/0.01A
- Reed switch K-factor: 0.1

Wait — DN40 Q1: 0.10 for ratio 160? 16.00/0.10 = 160 ✓. And Q2: 0.10×1.6=0.16 ✓. DN32 v1: Q1 = 10/160 = 0.0625 ✓, Q2 = 0.0625×1.6 = 0.1 ✓. v2: Q1 = 6.3/100 = 0.063 ✓, Q2 = 0.063×1.6 = 0.1008 ≈ 0.101 ✓. DN40 v2: Q1 = 10/100 = 0.1 ✓, Q2 = 0.16 ✓. Good.

Now, how to model the model family? Each DN has 2 variants (R160 and R100). So models could be:

DN15-R160, DN15-R100, DN20-R160, DN20-R100, DN25-R160, DN25-R100, DN32-R160, DN32-R100, DN40-R160, DN40-R100 — 10 models.

Model IDs: e.g. "DN15_R160" or "DN15 R160". I'll use "DN15-R160" style.

Then characteristics.model_level entries:
- nominal_diameter_dn: mm, values per model
- overload_flowrate_q4: m³/h
- permanent_flowrate_q3: m³/h
- transitional_flowrate_q2: m³/h
- minimum_flowrate_q1: m³/h
- ratio_q3_q1: dimensionless
- length_of_horizontal_water_meter: mm (DN15: ranges 115–165, DN20: 165–190, DN25: 175–210; DN32: 260; DN40: 300)
- connection_type_screw_thread_size: string (G3/4B, G1B, G11/4B for DN15-25; G1 1/2B, G2B for DN32-40)
- reed_switch_k_factor: impulse/L (DN15-25: 1/0.1 → value "1/0.1"? Hmm, that's the two variants: R160 → 1 impulse/L, R100 → 0.1 impulse/L. Actually K-factor 1/0.1 means 1 or 0.1 impulse/L. For DN32-40 it's 0.1. Hmm, is it per variant? The K-factor for the reed transmitter, probably selectable. For DN15-25 it's "1/0.1" and DN32-40 "0.1". I could make it model_level: for DN15-25 models value "1/0.1" and for DN32-40 value 0.1. Or type_level. Since it differs between the two tables, I could put in model_level with values per model. Let me put it as model_level: attribute reed_switch_k_factor, unit impulse/L, values: DN15-R160: "1/0.1"? Hmm, that doesn't cleanly map per variant. Simpler: type_level not possible since tables differ. I'll do model_level with the value as printed for each model ("1/0.1" for DN15-25 models, 0.1 for DN32-40 models). Actually, as a string "1/0.1" it might mean "1 or 0.1". Keep as string.

Type-level characteristics (common):
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6 (dimensionless)
- ratio_q4_q3: 1.25
- accuracy_class: 2
- mpe_lower_flowrate_zone: ±5% → value: 5, unit "%", with note ±? The structured value: {"value": {"min": -5, "max": 5}, "unit_symbol": "%"}? Hmm. The rule says numbers not strings, decimal point. For ±5% I could do value: 5, unit "%", and keep sign in... there's no sign field. Maybe value: "±5%"? The rules say numbers not strings for numbers. Range {min:-5, max:5} captures ±. I'll use {min: -5, max: 5}, unit "%". Hmm, but is that over-interpretation? ±5% means range −5% to +5%. That's a reasonable representation. Alternatively value: 5, unit "%". I think {min:-5,max:5} is fine.

Actually, let me be careful. MPE is ±5% for lower zone; upper zone: ±2% for water ≤30°C, ±3% for water >30°C. These are config_level entries with axis "water_temperature":
- attribute: mpe_upper_flowrate_zone, axis: water_temperature, values: [{condition: "≤30°C", value: 2, unit "%", sign ±}, {condition: ">30°C", value: 3, unit "%"}]

Hmm, the config_level value form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. I'll use value: {min: -2, max: 2}? That gets noisy. Maybe simpler: value: 2 with unit "%" and mention ± via... The schema doesn't have a sign field. I could put value: "±2%" as string — but rules say numbers, not strings. Hmm. I'll use {min:-2,max:2} and {min:-3,max:3} to represent ±. For the condition, "≤ 30 °C" — condition strings are fine.

- temperature_class: "T30 and T50" (string values)
- water_pressure_class: "MAP 16"
- pressure_loss_class: "ΔP 63" → string "DP63"? Keep as "ΔP 63" — hmm, no LaTeX restriction; Δ is a Unicode char, fine. I'll use "ΔP 63".
- indicating_range: for DN15-25: "9999,9999/99999,999" — this is European decimal commas: 9999.9999 / 99999.999 m³. Two variants of indicating range. For DN32-40: 99999.999. Hmm. This is model-dependent: DN15-25 has two ranges (probably per R160/R100 variant? or per resolution). Resolution: 0.00001/0.0001 for DN15-25 and 0.0001 for DN32-40. Indicating range 9999.9999 corresponds to resolution 0.00001 (5 decimal-ish), 99999.999 to 0.0001. So per variant: hmm, not clearly mapped. The "9999,9999/99999,999" is a list of two values. Could be model_level with value as printed string? Rules: lists of values are model matrix, but here the mapping to models isn't given. I think safest: type_level? No, they differ between the two tables (DN15-25 vs DN32-40). I could put into model_level with value strings per model group, but which variant gets which? Unknown.

Option: put indicating_range and resolution as config-level with axis "indicating device variant"? Not clearly stated. Alternative: record them in matrix_tables (preserving the tables) and put the unambiguous values in model_level/type_level, and for indicating range/resolution use string values as printed.

Actually the schema allows model_level values: {model, value}. I could assign indicating_range "9999.9999/99999.999" to DN15-25 models and "99999.999" to DN32-40 models, as strings (since decimal-comma conversion: 9999,9999 → 9999.9999). Rules say convert decimal commas. As a pair of alternatives "9999.9999/99999.999" — keep as string since it's a slash-separated list. Hmm, but the rules say lists of values are model matrices... but we can't disambiguate. I'll keep as string with a footnote-free representation. Actually, maybe treat resolution "0.00001/0.0001" as string too.

Alternatively, model-level per DN group:
- indicating_range_m3: value "9999.9999/99999.999" for DN15/20/25 models; "99999.999" for DN32/40 models.
- resolution_indicating_device_m3: "0.00001/0.0001" for DN15/20/25; 0.0001 for DN32/40.

Hmm wait, actually maybe I can infer: The two indicating ranges might correspond to the two registrations? Not stated. Keep string.

- flow_profile_sensitivity_classes: "U0 D0" → value "U0 D0", could split into upstream U0 and downstream D0. Keep one string "U0 D0".
- orientation_limitation: "No limitation"
- reed_switch_power_supply: Max. 24V/0.01A → split:
  - reed_switch_max_voltage: 24, V
  - reed_switch_max_current: 0.01, A
- temperature_class etc.

Now the model_level entries — I'll create models:
DN15-R160, DN15-R100, DN20-R160, DN20-R100, DN25-R160, DN25-R100, DN32-R160, DN32-R100, DN40-R160, DN40-R100.

Model-level attributes:
1. nominal_diameter_dn (mm): DN15: 15 (both variants), ..., DN40: 40.
2. overload_flowrate_q4 (m³/h): DN15-R160: 3.13; DN15-R100: 2.00; DN20-R160: 5.00; DN20-R100: 3.13; DN25-R160: 7.88; DN25-R100: 5.00; DN32-R160: 12.50; DN32-R100: 7.88; DN40-R160: 20.00; DN40-R100: 12.50.
3. permanent_flowrate_q3 (m³/h): DN15-R160: 2.50; DN15-R100: 1.60; DN20-R160: 4.00; DN20-R100: 2.5; DN25-R160: 6.30; DN25-R100: 4.00; DN32-R160: 10.00; DN32-R100: 6.30; DN40-R160: 16.00; DN40-R100: 10.00.
4. transitional_flowrate_q2 (m³/h): DN15-R160: 0.25 (as printed; hmm — should I keep 0.25? The printed is 0.25. Given Q1=0.0156 and ratio 1.6, expected 0.025. I'll keep as printed 0.25... but that seems wrong. The instruction: don't fabricate; extract as given. I'll extract 0.25. Hmm, but is it maybe that the OCR dropped a leading zero? Possibly. But I can't verify. Keep as printed.) Actually wait — let me reconsider. DN15-R100: Q1=0.016 → Q2=0.0256≈0.026 ✓ printed 0.026. DN15-R160 printed 0.25 — expected 0.025. Likely OCR missed a 0. But I follow "don't fabricate" and keep 0.25. Hmm, this is a judgment call. The rules say extract faithfully. OK.

DN20-R160: 0.04; DN20-R100: 0.04; DN25-R160: 0.63 (as printed; expected 0.063); DN25-R100: 0.064; DN32-R160: 0.10; DN32-R100: 0.101; DN40-R160: 0.16; DN40-R100: 0.16.

Hmm, DN25-R160 Q2 = 0.63 as printed — inconsistent with Q1=0.0394. Likely OCR for 0.063. Keep as printed. Similarly DN25-R100 Q1 = 0.004 as printed (expected 0.04). Keep 0.004. Hmm, that gives ratio Q3/Q1 = 1000 for DN25-R100 which contradicts printed ratio 100. It's an OCR artifact. I'll keep printed values. Actually... let me think about whether to normalize. The instruction 8: "Don't fabricate. If a field is not present in the markdown, omit it." It doesn't say to correct OCR errors. Faithful extraction = keep 0.63 and 0.004. OK.

5. minimum_flowrate_q1 (m³/h): DN15-R160: 0.0156; DN15-R100: 0.016; DN20-R160: 0.025; DN20-R100: 0.025; DN25-R160: 0.0394; DN25-R100: 0.004; DN32-R160: 0.0625; DN32-R100: 0.063; DN40-R160: 0.10; DN40-R100: 0.10.
6. ratio_q3_q1: 160 for -R160 variants; 100 for -R100 variants.
7. length_of_horizontal_water_meter (mm): DN15: {115,165}; DN20: {165,190}; DN25: {175,210}; DN32: 260; DN40: 300.
8. connection_type_screw_thread_size (string): DN15: "G3/4B"; DN20: "G1B"; DN25: "G11/4B"; DN32: "G1 1/2B"; DN40: "G2B".
9. reed_switch_k_factor (impulse/L): DN15-25 models: "1/0.1"; DN32-40 models: 0.1.

Type-level:
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6
- ratio_q4_q3: 1.25
- accuracy_class: 2
- mpe_lower_flowrate_zone: {min:-5,max:5} %
- temperature_class: "T30 and T50" — maybe list? value string "T30 and T50". Or value: ["T30","T50"]? Schema says value is number | {min,max} | string. Use "T30 and T50".
- water_pressure_class: "MAP 16"
- pressure_loss_class: "ΔP 63"
- flow_profile_sensitivity_classes: "U0 D0"

- temperature_class breakdown.

Config-level:
- mpe_upper_flowrate_zone with axis "water_temperature": [{condition: "water temperature ≤ 30 °C", value: {min:-2,max:2}, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "water temperature > 30 °C", value: {min:-3,max:3}, unit_symbol: "%"}]

Model-dependent indicating range and resolution: I'll add to model_level:
- indicating_range: value "9999.9999/99999.999" (string) for DN15/20/25 models; "99999.999" for DN32/40. unit m³.
- resolution_of_indicating_device: "0.00001/0.0001" for DN15-25; 0.0001 for DN32-40. unit m³.

Hmm, but with 10 models each, that's 10 entries per attribute — fine.

Actually, should I include both matrix_tables AND model_level? Rule 4 says for explicit 2-D tables: "EXTRACT as matrix_tables[] AND populate model_family.models and characteristics.model_level". Yes, do both.

matrix_tables: two tables:
1. "Basic technical data of water meters type PD97TRP DN15 to DN25" — columns: nominal_diameter_dn, overload_flowrate_q4, permanent_flowrate_q3, transitional_flowrate_q2, minimum_flowrate_q1, ratio_q3_q1, ... rows per variant? The original table has DN rows and attribute rows with 6 value columns (2 per DN). I'll restructure rows per DN-variant:
   columns: ["model", "nominal_diameter_dn", "overload_flowrate_q4", "permanent_flowrate_q3", "transitional_flowrate_q2", "minimum_flowrate_q1", "ratio_q3_q1"]
   rows: 6 rows.
   
   Plus common attributes... include as columns? The table has shared rows: ratio_q2_q1, ratio_q4_q3, accuracy_class, MPE, temperature class, pressure classes, pressure-loss class, indicating range, resolution, flow profile sensitivity, orientation, length, connection, reed supply, K-factor. I could include all columns in the matrix table rows:

   columns: ["model", "nominal_diameter_dn", "overload_flowrate_q4_m3_h", "permanent_flowrate_q3_m3_h", "transitional_flowrate_q2_m3_h", "minimum_flowrate_q1_m3_h", "ratio_q3_q1", "length_mm", "connection_thread", "indicating_range_m3", "resolution_m3", "reed_switch_k_factor_impulse_l"]

   Hmm, that's getting complex but preserves data. The schema for matrix_tables: name, columns[], rows[] (object per row), description, footnotes[]. column_units shown in example. I'll include column_units.

   Rows for table 1:
   - {model: "DN15-R160", nominal_diameter_dn: 15, q4: 3.13, q3: 2.50, q2: 0.25, q1: 0.0156, ratio_q3_q1: 160, length: {min:115,max:165}, connection: "G3/4B", indicating_range: "9999.9999/99999.999", resolution: "0.00001/0.0001", k_factor: "1/0.1"}
   - {model: "DN15-R100", 15, 2.00, 1.60, 0.026, 0.016, 100, ...}
   - {model: "DN20-R160", 20, 5.00, 4.00, 0.04, 0.025, 160, {165,190}, "G1B", ...}
   - {model: "DN20-R100", 20, 3.13, 2.5, 0.04, 0.025, 100, ...}
   - {model: "DN25-R160", 25, 7.88, 6.30, 0.63, 0.0394, 160, {175,210}, "G11/4B", ...}
   - {model: "DN25-R100", 25, 5.00, 4.00, 0.064, 0.004, 100, ...}

   For rows, values can be plain numbers (matrix_tables rows don't need the strict structured-value shape per the R137 example — example shows plain numbers). Good, simpler.

2. Table 2 rows:
   - {model: "DN32-R160", 32, 12.50, 10.00, 0.10, 0.0625, 160, 260, "G1 1/2B", "99999.999", 0.0001, 0.1}
   - {model: "DN32-R100", 32, 7.88, 6.30, 0.101, 0.063, 100, 260, "G1 1/2B", ...}
   - {model: "DN40-R160", 40, 20.00, 16.00, 0.16, 0.10, 160, 300, "G2B", ...}
   - {model: "DN40-R100", 40, 12.50, 10.00, 0.16, 0.10, 100, 300, ...}
